verses.text: Afterward Nahash, king of the Ammonites, died, and his son took his place.
David said, "I'll show kindness to Hanun son of Nahash because his father showed kindness to me." So he sent messengers into Ammonite territory to offer Hanun condolences for his father's death.
But the Ammonite leaders said to Hanun, "Do you think David sent these men because he wants to honor your father? Haven't they come to scout the land, spy on it, and overthrow it?"
So Hanun seized David's servants, shaved them, cut their clothes off at the buttocks, and sent them away.
When David heard how the men had been treated, he sent people to meet them because they had been deeply humiliated. The king told them, "Stay in Jericho until your beards grow back. Then come home."
When the Ammonites realized how badly they had offended David, Hanun and his people sent a thousand talents of silver to hire chariots and horsemen from Mesopotamia, Aram-maacah, and Zobah.
They hired thirty-two thousand chariots, along with the king of Maacah and his people, who came and camped near Medeba. The Ammonites gathered from their towns and came out for battle.
When David heard, he sent Joab with the whole army of his best fighters.
The Ammonites lined up for battle at the city gate, while the kings who had come stayed apart in the open field.
Joab saw that he was facing battle on two fronts, so he picked some of Israel's best men and lined them up against the Syrians.
He put his brother Abishai in charge of the rest of the troops, who lined up against the Ammonites.
Joab said, "If the Syrians are too strong for me, come help me. If the Ammonites are too strong for you, I'll come help you.
Be brave. Let's stand strong for our people and the cities of our God. May the LORD do what seems good to him."
Joab and his troops advanced to fight the Syrians, and the Syrians ran from him.
When the Ammonites saw the Syrians flee, they ran from Joab's brother Abishai and retreated into the city. Then Joab went back to Jerusalem.
When the Syrians saw that Israel had defeated them, they sent messengers to bring in Syrians from beyond the Euphrates. Shophach, the commander of Hadadezer's army, led them.
When David heard, he gathered all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and took up positions against them. The Syrians met him in battle.
The Syrians ran from Israel. David killed seven thousand Syrian chariot drivers and forty thousand foot soldiers, as well as Shophach, their commander.
When Hadadezer's subjects saw that Israel had defeated them, they made peace with David and became his subjects. The Syrians gave the Ammonites no more help.
